blocking_issues: The mapping claims BN_STATUS has only source values Registered and Cancelled and maps Cancelled to deregistered, but validator evidence shows raw BN_STATUS value "Deregistered" in multiple records. Those records are quarantined rather than semantically handled, so the declared status mapping is not complete for the supplied source and loses source claims.

The mapping emits entity.status from a field explicitly documented as the registration status of the business name, while the target field is entity.status and the mapping's subject_role is business_name_holder. The configuration does not provide a distinct business-name status field or an explicit target-level qualification that entity.status is a status observation about the business-name subject rather than the underlying legal entity. Given the ontology's distinction between entities and trading names, this creates a material subject/grain ambiguity.
warnings: The partial mapping of BN_NAME to entity.trading_name is defensible as a business-name/trading-name label, but the source does not establish that it is a legal name, the holder's trading name, or a unique legal entity; this limitation is disclosed.

BN_ABN is explicitly an external ATO identifier, may be suppressed/null, may relate to multiple business names, and does not by itself establish unique holder ownership. Checksum validation is appropriate, but link confidence is not shown in the supplied mapping and should not be implied.

BN_REG_DT and BN_CANCEL_DT are correctly left unmapped rather than being treated as legal-entity dates or deregistration. BN_STATE_NUM and BN_STATE_OF_REG are also reasonably left unmapped because no supported target fields are present.
The publication proxy is a defensible observation-time fallback, but it is not the source's explicit statement time; observed_at_field is null and this should remain clearly labeled as a proxy.
No address, branch/service-location, reporting-group, legal-name, entity-type, ACN, website, or industry-code mapping is supported by the supplied documentation; not mapping them is appropriate.

The source documentation says currently registered names plus deregistered names for the prior 12 months, while the mapping wording says recent deregistered names without specifying the 12-month retention. This is a minor documentation limitation, not by itself a blocker.

The validation report says 300 discovery records but 250 output records and 29 quarantined fields; the supplied evidence does not establish whether the 50-record difference is expected engine behavior. This merits human review, but should not be treated as a semantic defect without more evidence.
The confidence values are plausible but uncalibrated judgements, and the source_reliability score is not substantiated by a formal calibration method; this is acceptable if treated as provisional.

blocking_issues: The mapping emits entity.trading_name and entity.abn as observations without a declared deterministic linkage/key strategy between the business-name row, the BN_NAME claim, and the ABN claim. The source grain is a business-name registration record, while the ontology fields are entity-level; the mapping correctly acknowledges this mismatch but does not prevent an ABN from being interpreted as the legal entity owning the trading name. This is a semantic subject-ownership/linkage gap, not merely wording.

The mapping's observed_at policy uses a publication_proxy timestamp, but the supplied source metadata identifies that value as a publication proxy for the dataset and does not establish that it is the time the source stated each individual row. The envelope requires observed_at as when the source stated the claim; this limitation needs an explicit, reviewable treatment rather than silently treating the publication proxy as record observation time.
warnings: The BN_NAME-to-entity.trading_name mapping is defensible as a deliberately partial name claim, and it explicitly avoids legal_name; however, the target ontology has no business-name-specific object, so the remaining entity-level representation is inherently lossy.

BN_ABN is documented as an ABR/ATO identifier, may be suppressed or absent, and can occur across multiple business names. ABN checksum validation is appropriate, but validation does not prove holder ownership or uniqueness.

Leaving BN_STATUS, BN_REG_DT, BN_CANCEL_DT, BN_STATE_NUM, and BN_STATE_OF_REG unmapped is appropriate given the available ontology and the need not to turn business-name registration semantics into legal-entity status, dates, or address claims.

The source documentation says currently registered names plus deregistered names for the prior 12 months; the mapping does not appear to expose a filter or valid-time interpretation for that retention window. This is a disclosed source limitation, not a blocker unless consumers require historical completeness.

The supplied discovery evidence has 300 records, while validation reports 250 records and 452 observations; the discrepancy is unexplained in the presented material. It may reflect engine handling or record selection, but should be reconciled by the validator/human.
Confidence values are plausible provisional judgements, but link_confidence is not supplied despite the unresolved entity linkage; field confidence should not substitute for link confidence.
No unsupported constants, addresses, legal names, entity types, reporting groups, or current/historic name transitions are invented. REGISTER_NAME is correctly unmapped.

ASIC help file p.8: BN_NAME is the business name/name used or to be used in relation to one or more businesses; it is not defined as the holder's legal name. BN_STATUS is status for the Business Name.

ASIC help file pp.9-10: BN_REG_DT and BN_CANCEL_DT describe when the business name started/ceased; BN_STATE_NUM and BN_STATE_OF_REG are former-regulator historical business-name details; BN_ABN is an ATO/ABR ABN with null/suppression conditions.
Discovery records: eight-column tab-delimited rows, BN_NAME values with leading spaces, Registered statuses, DD/MM/YYYY registration dates, blank cancellation/state fields, and 11-digit ABN strings.

Ontology: entity.trading_name, entity.abn, and required observation envelope; no business-name-specific status, cancellation, former state number, or registration-history fields; link_confidence is a separate confidence concept.
Trusted engine semantics: trim/digits/ABN validation is implementation-valid, but does not establish semantic ownership or legal-entity identity.

blocking_issues: The mapping emits BN_ABN as entity.abn without an explicit exact-membership filter for this field. The documentation says BN_ABN can be NULL when an ABN was issued by a previous regulator and not recorded with ASIC, when multiple ABNs exist, or when suppressed; however, a populated value is explicitly described as an ABN. The supplied engine semantics make the ABN transform checksum-validating, so this is semantically defensible only for valid values, but the mapping does not establish that the ABN identifies the legal entity or holder. Given the ontology's entity.abn meaning and the declared subject grain business_name_holder, emitting it as a legal-entity attribute risks asserting ownership/linkage that the source does not prove.

The mapping emits BN_NAME as entity.trading_name while its subject is a business-name registration, not a legal entity. This is a reasonable partial representation, but the target entity field requires an entity interpretation and the mapping does not define a separate business-name subject/object or a deterministic legal-entity link. It therefore risks presenting the registered business name as a trading name of a canonical entity rather than preserving it solely as a source business-name observation.
warnings: BN_STATUS, BN_REG_DT, and BN_CANCEL_DT are correctly left unmapped to legal-entity status/dates; this is a deliberate limitation, not a defect.
REGISTER_NAME, BN_STATE_NUM, and BN_STATE_OF_REG are appropriately unmapped; the latter two are historical former-regulator business-name data, not current service-location addresses.
No address, reporting-group, legal name, ACN, or holder type is claimed; that partiality is supported by the source.
Trimming BN_NAME is supported by the sample leading spaces, but whitespace normalization should not otherwise alter the source spelling.

The publication proxy is explicitly disclosed and is not a row-level statement timestamp. The source snapshot is described as weekly/current names plus deregistered names for 12 months, so historic coverage is limited and not a complete history.

The validation pass is syntactic/operational only. The reported discovery/validation record-count discrepancy is disclosed and needs reconciliation, although it does not by itself prove a mapping error.

Confidence values are appropriately separated from validation and are stated as provisional; however, 0.91 field confidence for entity.abn may overstate confidence in the semantic entity-link claim even if confidence in parsing the ABN value is high.
evidence_checked: ASIC Business Names Dataset Help File pp.3-5: snapshot of the Business Names register; currently registered names and deregistered names for the prior 12 months; not all register information.

ASIC Business Names Dataset Help File pp.8-10: BN_NAME is a business name used in relation to one or more businesses; BN_ABN is an ATO/ABR ABN with documented NULL conditions; BN_STATUS and dates concern the Business Name; former state fields concern prior business-name regulators.

Discovery rows: all supplied rows have the eight documented columns; BN_NAME has leading spaces; statuses shown are Registered; dates use DD/MM/YYYY; BN_ABN values are populated 11-digit strings in samples.

Ontology: entity.legal_name is as registered and distinct from entity.trading_name; entity.abn is an Australian Business Number for an entity; no canonical business-name-registration or reporting-group field exists.
Trusted engine semantics: trim/digits/ABN validation behavior and the distinction between source parsing and semantic linkage.
Previous mapping and validator output: two mapped fields, unmapped source fields, publication-proxy timestamp policy, 250 validated records/452 observations, and no parse errors.
